subject: About the cpu time of calling inla

messages.author: 12836e6a447153b7
messages.subject: About the cpu time of calling inla
parts:
Dear all,
 
I have run many simulations using spde2 model and I found a confusing thing about the computing time for calling inla.
For the same number of observations and predictions(stk_est, stk_prd), I thought the time depends on generally the n.spde (mesh$n) saying the larger n.spde, the longer cpu time.
But I found that sometimes, I have nearly the same number of observations and predictions but different values, the cpu time calling inla with less mesh$n can be longer than that with more mesh$n..
I wonder why?
 
Thanks a lot!
 
Ming

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] About the cpu time of calling inla
parts:
On 30/06/14 15:18, ming li wrote:
> Dear all,
> I have run many simulations using spde2 model and I found a confusing
> thing about the computing time for calling inla.
> For the same number of observations and predictions(stk_est, stk_prd), I
> thought the time depends on generally the n.spde (mesh$n) saying the
> larger n.spde, the longer cpu time.
> But I found that sometimes, I have nearly the same number of
> observations and predictions but different values, the cpu time calling
> inla with less mesh$n can be longer than that with more mesh$n..

Have you checked the parameter estimates, and used verbose=TRUE to
check the parameter optimisation? The time per likelihood evaluation
should be monotone in the mesh size, but the number of iterations
needed doesn't necessarily behave in a predictable way.

The precise structure of the model also has an effect, and it sounds
like you changed more than only the mesh size (e.g. the locations of
the data points affects the parameter estimation, and hence the
optimiser).

Finally, inla uses different computing strategies for different model
sizes, and it may be that it doesn't always use the optimal strategy.

Finn
